69:| R-BOOT-4 | The firmware runs in fwtest without a fault, halt or hang, touches nothing fwtest does not model, and leaves core 1 stopped (until M5; since M5 core 1 runs the FM engine's loop and nothing else, R-FM-6). (The test builds of R-IRQ-3 and R-IRQ-4 halt on purpose, and touch nothing unmodelled either.) | M0d, M5 | C-FW-SUITE, C-UNIT |
96:| R-AUD-1 | The audio output (HW-43 to HW-46): `JL_ALNK0` plays a buffer in RAM of two halves, each a block of 64 stereo frames (`LEN` 128 words), 24-bit samples sign-extended in 32-bit words, at 24 MHz / 544 = 44 117.647 Hz; each finished half raises source 11, whose handler, at the lowest priority, has the engine refill that half while the other plays. Every block fwtest finishes is filled once (the audio record's count against `ipb.csv`), no two block ends are more than a block apart, left equals right, and the firmware touches nothing fwtest doesn't model. Core 1 stays parked (R-BOOT-4) until M5, when it renders half the voices (R-FM-6). | M4, M5 | C-FW-SUITE, C-UNIT |
98:| R-AUD-3 | Underruns are never silent: a half that goes by without a refill, or a refill still going when the next half finishes, is counted in the audio record and reported on the debug channel (`AUDIO UNDERRUN nnnn`, the count so far). A test build late for one block in 64 shows each counted and reported once while the output goes on. The firmware has none over 10 s of the heaviest input (until M5 M3's scripts: all seven encoders turning, a chord, a pot sweep, every 500 ms, with every voice and the test tone playing; since M5 R-FM-6's), and every tick interval stays within 24 000 ± 24 time base ticks meanwhile. | M4, M5 | C-FW-SUITE, C-UNIT |
102:| R-AUD-7 | Where the output is exactly deterministic, it is compared exactly: a note and the test tone, the whole output, against a golden WAV (since M5 made by the FM engine; R-FM-8 for the test patches). | M4, M5 | C-FW-SUITE |
103:| R-FM-1 | The FM engine's operators (M5; firmware/src/fm.c): six a voice, each a 32-bit phase accumulator reading our own sine (a 1 024-step table from its series, interpolated linearly), its frequency a ratio of the note's (x 1/256) or fixed (1/4 Hz), a fine detune in cents and an output level; one feedback operator per algorithm. Phase modulation as Chowning's FM: a two-operator patch (test patch 1, a modulator at the note's frequency into a carrier at 6 times it, index pi/2) gives sidebands at (6 + n) f whose shares of the whole are \|J_n(pi/2)\| within 0.05 dB for n from -4 to 4 and 0.5 dB for ±5 (where the folded -7 lies), measured by a least-squares fit at the known frequencies, and their total within 0.01 dB of the carrier's level. | M5 | C-FW-SUITE, C-UNIT |
104:| R-FM-2 | Our own ten algorithms (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M5, with diagrams), each operator's output going to one lower operator or to the output: stacks, parallel carriers and branches; ALGORITHM selects one for new notes, a patch sets its own. The carriers share the output (divided by how many sound). Aliasing is kept low by design: an operator at or above half the rate is silent; a modulator's index is held to what Carson's rule lets its carrier's band fit below half the rate; feedback uses the mean of the last two outputs. | M5 | review; C-FW-SUITE (R-FM-8) |
105:| R-FM-3 | Envelopes: per operator, attack (linear in gain), decay 1, decay 2 (to a held level) and release (linear in dB), and one for pitch (three rates, four levels); rates as time codes (2^(t/8) ms a stage's whole range) and levels in 0.753 dB steps; stage changes carry the rest of the block on, gains are interpolated a sample at a time. Test patch 2: each stage ends within a block (1.45 ms) of its nominal time, falls within 3% of its rate, holds within 0.1 dB of its level, the attack is half-way at half its time (±0.03), no click. /*
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
 * SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
 *
 * The audio layer (M4): the output, double-buffered and driven by its
 * interrupt, and the one callback a sound engine implements. This is the
 * API engines are written against, beside input.h; keep it small and
 * stable (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M4, "The audio API").
 *
 * - The engine is one function, audio_engine_fn. The audio layer calls it
 *   once a block, from the output's interrupt, to fill the half of the
 *   buffer that has just finished playing while the other half plays.
 * - A block is AUDIO_FRAMES stereo frames: 2 * AUDIO_FRAMES words, left
 *   then right, each a 24-bit signed sample, sign-extended to 32 bits,
 *   within -AUDIO_FULL .. AUDIO_FULL (HW-44). The engine writes them
 *   straight into the buffer the output plays from: nothing is copied or
 *   converted after it, so it must write every word and stay in range.
 * - The rate is AUDIO_RATE_NUM / AUDIO_RATE_DEN frames a second (HW-45):
 *   44 117.647 Hz, not 44 100.
 * - Between blocks the engine reads the panel's input events with
 *   input_read_audio() (input.h), from inside its callback: the same
 *   events, in the same order, as main's input_read(), from a queue of
 *   their own. input_value() gives any control's present state.
 * - The callback runs in an interrupt at the lowest priority: the tick
 *   and the input scan may interrupt it, main never does. It must finish
 *   within one block (AUDIO_FRAMES / rate, 1.451 ms); a block it is late
 *   for is an underrun, counted and reported on the debug channel
 *   (sb_audio.underruns).
 */

#ifndef AUDIO_H
#define AUDIO_H

#include "sb.h"

#define AUDIO_FRAMES     64u           /* stereo frames a block */
#define AUDIO_RATE_NUM   24000000u     /* frames a second: 24 MHz / 544 (HW-45) */
#define AUDIO_RATE_DEN   544u
#define AUDIO_FULL       0x7FFFFF      /* 24-bit full scale */

/* Fills frames stereo frames at out: out[2n] left, out[2n + 1] right. */
typedef void (*audio_engine_fn)(s32 *out, u32 frames);

/* Starts the output with silence and engine as its engine; main calls it
 * once, before interrupts are on. */
void audio_start(audio_engine_fn engine);
void audio_block(void) __attribute__((interrupt("")));

/* The audio record: counters, at a fixed place in RAM right after the
 * input record (firmware/app.ld), for the tests to capture with fwtest's
 * --ram (tools/fw-suite.py reads this layout). Times are in time base
 * ticks (24 a microsecond). */
#define AUDIO_MARKER     0x34445541u   /* "AUD4" in memory order */
struct sb_audio_record {
    u32 marker;       /* AUDIO_MARKER once the output runs */
    u32 start;        /* sb_ticks() when the output started */
    u32 blocks;       /* blocks the engine filled */
    u32 underruns;    /* blocks it was late for, or a half that went by */
    u32 fill_last;    /* the last block's fill: interrupt to engine done */
    u32 fill_max;     /* the longest */
    u32 dropped;      /* input events the engine's queue dropped (full) */
    u32 engine[9];    /* the engine's own (SYNTH_* below) */
};
extern volatile struct sb_audio_record sb_audio;

/* What the engine keeps in sb_audio.engine: M4's test instrument's
 * fields, kept by the FM engine since M5 (fm_play.c). */
#define SYNTH_VOICES_ON  0   /* voices sounding */
#define SYNTH_NOTES      1   /* notes started */
#define SYNTH_TONE       2   /* 1 while the test tone plays */
#define SYNTH_MASTER     3   /* the MASTER gain, 0 to 1 << 24 */
#define SYNTH_EVENTS     4   /* input events taken */
#define SYNTH_STOLEN     5   /* notes that took a voice still sounding */
#define SYNTH_OCTAVE     6   /* octave shift, -2 to 2, as stored (s32) */
#define SYNTH_FIRST_ON   7   /* sb_audio.blocks when the first note began */
#define SYNTH_LAST_OFF   8   /* sb_audio.blocks when a voice last went silent */


#endif

        self.assertIn("#define FM_PATCHES    %du" % len(fp.TEST_PATCHES), header)

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
import os
import re
import unittest

from tests.helpers import ROOT, load_tool

mm = load_tool("midi_model.py")


def run(*b):
    return mm.parse(b)


class MidiModelTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-MIDI-1"""

    def test_running_status(self):
        p = run(0x90, 60, 100, 62, 90, 64, 0)
        self.assertEqual(p.log, [(0x90, 60, 100, 2), (0x90, 62, 90, 2), (0x90, 64, 0, 2)])

    def test_one_data_byte_messages(self):
        p = run(0xC3, 5, 6, 0xD0, 40)
        self.assertEqual(p.log, [(0xC3, 5, 0, 1), (0xC3, 6, 0, 1), (0xD0, 40, 0, 1)])

    def test_realtime_inside_a_message_changes_nothing(self):
        p = run(0x90, 0xF8, 60, 0xFE, 100, 0xFA, 61, 0xFC, 101)
        self.assertEqual(p.log, [(0xF8, 0, 0, 0), (0xFE, 0, 0, 0), (0x90, 60, 100, 2),
                                 (0xFA, 0, 0, 0), (0xFC, 0, 0, 0), (0x90, 61, 101, 2)])
        self.assertEqual(p.count["realtime"], 4)

    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="where the suite's outputs go (empty or new)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(os.path.join(ROOT, os.path.dirname(IMAGE)), exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(a.build, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, IMAGE))
    global START_SLACK
    size = os.path.join(a.build, "app.size")
    if os.path.exists(size):
        with open(size) as f:
            sizes = dict(l.split() for l in f if l.strip())
        print("image size: " + ", ".join("%s %s" % kv for kv in sizes.items()))
        START_SLACK = start_slack(int(sizes.get("bss", 0)))

    symbols = elf_symbols(os.path.join(a.build, "app.elf"))
    problems = build_tests(a.build)

    p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/fwtest", "suite", SUITE, "--out", out], cwd=ROOT,

    print(p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip())

        problems.append("fwtest suite exited %d" % p.returncode)

        path = os.path.join(out, name, "result.json")
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            problems.append("%s: no result.json" % name)
            continue

        if name in ("boot", "screen", "fault", "stray", "chords") and not result.get("golden"):
            problems.append("%s: no golden files compared" % name)
        case_dir = os.path.join(out, name)
        more, lines = [], []
        if name == "boot":
            more, lines = check_boot(case_dir, symbols)
        elif name in ("heartbeat", "heartbeat2") and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_heartbeat(case_dir, result)
            with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "ram-01c00000-%x-end.bin" % BEACON_LEN), "rb") as f:
                steady[name] = (result, beacon(f.read()))
            if len(steady) == 2:
                m, l = check_steady([steady["heartbeat"][0], steady["heartbeat2"][0]],
                                    [steady["heartbeat"][1], steady["heartbeat2"][1]])
                more, lines = more + m, lines + l
        elif name == "screen":
            more, lines = check_screen(case_dir)
        elif name == "flood" and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_flood(case_dir, result, os.path.join(out, "screen"))
        elif name == "fault":
            more, lines = check_halt(name, case_dir, HALT_STACK, 1)
        elif name == "stray":
            more, lines = check_halt(name, case_dir, HALT_STRAY, 127)
        elif name in INPUT_CHECKS and run.get("outcome") == EXPECT[name]:
            more, lines = INPUT_CHECKS[name](case_dir)
        elif name in AUDIO_CHECKS and run.get("outcome") == EXPECT[name]:
            try:
                more, lines = AUDIO_CHECKS[name](case_dir)
            except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
                more, lines = ["%s: %s" % (name, e)], []
        problems += more
        if lines:
            print("\n".join(lines))

    for prob in problems:
        print("FAIL: " + prob)
    print("fw suite: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Writes the fwtest scripts of M6a's MIDI cases (tests/fw/scripts/midi*.txt;
R-MIDI-*), and reads their byte streams back for tools/fw-suite.py.

  midi_scripts.py            writes every script
  midi_scripts.py --check    exits 1 if a committed script differs

A `midi` event's bytes arrive one every 320 us, the first 320 us after its
time (docs/HARNESS.md, "Scripts"); the writer never lets two `midi`
events overlap, so the bytes reach the firmware in the order written.
Streams that are long or random (a SysEx flood, garbage, the dense
stream) come from a fixed seed, so the scripts are the same every time.
"""

import os
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SCRIPTS = os.path.join(ROOT, "tests", "fw", "scripts")
BYTE_MS = 0.32
CHUNK = 32          # bytes per `midi` line


class Script:
    def __init__(self, name, about):
        self.name, self.about, self.lines, self.t = name, about, [], 0.0

    def at(self, ms):
        """The next event no earlier than ms (and after the last byte)."""
        self.t = max(self.t, ms)
        return self

    def wait(self, ms):
        self.t += ms
        return self

    def midi(self, *data):
        b = [x for d in data for x in (d if isinstance(d, (list, tuple, bytes)) else [d])]
        for i in range(0, len(b), CHUNK):
            part = b[i:i + CHUNK]
            self.lines.append("%-8s midi %s" % (fmt(self.t), " ".join("%02x" % x for x in part)))
            self.t = round(self.t + BYTE_MS * len(part), 3)
        return self

    def event(self, text):
        self.lines.append("%-8s %s" % (fmt(self.t), text))
        return self

    def text(self):
        head = ["# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT", "# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98", "#",
                "# Written by tools/midi_scripts.py; don't edit by hand.", "#"]
        head += ["# " + l if l else "#" for l in self.about.split("\n")]
        return "\n".join(head + ["#", "# time   event"] + self.lines) + "\n"


def fmt(ms):
    s = "%.3f" % ms
    return s.rstrip("0").rstrip(".")


def rng(seed):
    x = seed
    while True:
        x = (x * 1103515245 + 12345) & 0x7FFFFFFF
        yield x >> 16 & 0xFF


def on(note, vel, ch=0):
    return [0x90 | ch, note, vel]


def off(note, ch=0):
    return [0x80 | ch, note, 0x40]


def cc(n, v, ch=0):
    return [0xB0 | ch, n, v]


def bend(v, ch=0):
    return [0xE0 | ch, v & 0x7F, v >> 7]

    def text(self):
        head = ["# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT", "# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98", "#",
                "# Written by tools/midi_scripts.py; don't edit by hand.", "#"]
        head += ["# " + l if l else "#" for l in self.about.split("\n")]
        return "\n".join(head + ["#", "# time   event"] + self.lines) + "\n"


def fmt(ms):
    s = "%.3f" % ms
    return s.rstrip("0").rstrip(".")


def rng(seed):
    x = seed
    while True:
        x = (x * 1103515245 + 12345) & 0x7FFFFFFF
        yield x >> 16 & 0xFF


def on(note, vel, ch=0):
    return [0x90 | ch, note, vel]


def off(note, ch=0):
    return [0x80 | ch, note, 0x40]


def cc(n, v, ch=0):
    return [0xB0 | ch, n, v]


def bend(v, ch=0):
    return [0xE0 | ch, v & 0x7F, v >> 7]


# --- The cases ---------------------------------------------------------

def midimsg():
    s = Script("midimsg", "midimsg (R-MIDI-2, R-MIDI-3): every message the engine takes, on\n"
               "channel 1, test patch 0 then 8 by program change. Ends with every\n"
               "note off and every voice idle.")
    s.at(100).midi(on(60, 100)).wait(150).midi(off(60))
    s.wait(150).midi(on(62, 90)).wait(150).midi(on(62, 0))          # velocity 0 is an off
    s.wait(150).midi(on(64, 127)).wait(50).midi(bend(16383)).wait(100).midi(bend(0))
    s.wait(100).midi(bend(8192)).wait(50).midi(cc(1, 127)).wait(200).midi(cc(1, 0)).midi(off(64))
    # The bend range by RPN 0: 12 semitones, then a bend to the top.
    s.wait(100).midi(cc(101, 0), cc(100, 0), cc(6, 12), cc(101, 127), cc(100, 127))
    s.wait(50).midi(on(65, 100)).midi(bend(16383)).wait(100).midi(bend(8192)).midi(off(65))
    s.wait(100).midi(cc(7, 64), cc(11, 100)).midi(on(67, 100)).wait(100).midi(off(67))
    s.wait(100).midi(cc(7, 127), cc(11, 127))
    # The knobs' controllers, then back to the middle.
    s.wait(50).midi(cc(16, 127), cc(17, 0), cc(18, 0), cc(19, 127))
    s.wait(50).midi(cc(16, 64), cc(17, 64), cc(18, 64), cc(19, 64))
    # All notes off, all sound off.
    s.wait(100).midi(on(60, 100), on(64, 100), on(67, 100)).wait(100).midi(cc(123, 0))
    s.wait(200).midi(on(60, 100), on(64, 100)).wait(100).midi(cc(120, 0)).midi(off(60), off(64))
    # A program change: test patch 8; one past the patches is ignored.
    s.wait(200).midi([0xC0, 8]).midi([0xC0, 9]).midi(on(60, 100)).wait(100).midi(off(60))
    # Aftertouch is taken and ignored.
    s.wait(100).midi([0xD0, 50], [0xA0, 60, 50])
    return s


def midirun():
    s = Script("midirun", "midirun (R-MIDI-1): running status and realtime bytes everywhere: a\n"
               "chord in running status with clock, start, stop and active sensing\n"
               "between and inside its messages; then notes off, each byte apart.")
    s.at(100).midi(0x90, 60, 0xF8, 100, 64, 0xFE, 100, 0xF8, 67, 100, 0xFA)
    s.wait(200).midi(0xF8, 0x90, 0xF8, 60, 0xF8, 0, 0xF8, 64, 0xF8, 0, 0xFC, 67, 0xFE, 0)
    s.wait(100).midi(0xB0, 1, 0xF8, 64, 7, 0xF8, 127, 1, 0)       # running status on a controller
    for _ in range(4):
        s.wait(50).midi([0xF8] * 6, 0xFE)
    return s


def midisysex():
    r = rng(7)
    s = Script("midisysex", "midisysex (R-MIDI-1): a SysEx flood: 40 short SysEx messages,\n"
               "one of 6 000 bytes (past the limit), one cut short by a note on,\n"
               "realtime inside them, and an EOX with no SysEx; notes play after each.")
    s.at(100)
    for i in range(40):
        s.midi(0xF0, [next(r) & 0x7F for _ in range(8 + i % 9)], 0xF8, 0xF7)
    s.midi(on(60, 100)).wait(50).midi(off(60))
    s.wait(20).midi(0xF0, [next(r) & 0x7F for _ in range(6000)], 0xF7)
    s.midi(on(62, 100)).wait(50).midi(off(62))
    s.wait(20).midi(0xF0, 1, 2, 3, on(64, 100)).wait(50).midi(off(64))
    s.wait(20).midi(0xF7, on(65, 100)).wait(50).midi(off(65))
    return s


def midijunk():
    r = rng(1234)
    s = Script("midijunk", "midijunk (R-MIDI-1): truncated messages and 3 000 random bytes, then a\n"
               "reset of what the junk may have set (all sound off, controllers,\n"
               "the pedal, poly mode, patch 0 on each channel), then a clean note.")
    s.at(100).midi(0x90, 60).midi(0xB0).midi(0xE0, 5).midi(0xC0).midi(0x80, 60, 0)
    s.wait(20).midi([next(r) for _ in range(3000)])
    for ch in range(16):
        s.midi(cc(120, 0, ch), cc(121, 0, ch), cc(64, 0, ch), cc(127, 0, ch), [0xC0 | ch, 0],
               cc(7, 127, ch), cc(16, 64, ch), cc(17, 64, ch), cc(18, 64, ch), cc(19, 64, ch),
               cc(101, 0, ch), cc(100, 0, ch), cc(6, 2, ch))
    s.wait(50).midi(on(60, 100)).wait(100).midi(off(60))
    return s


def mididense():
    s = Script("mididense", "mididense (R-MIDI-4): the wire full for 6 s: 16 notes held, each struck\n"
               "again in turn (running status, note on then off at velocity 0),\n"
               "the mod wheel and pitch bend moving between; then every note off.")
    notes = list(range(48, 80, 2))
    s.at(100).midi(0x90, [x for n in notes for x in (n, 100)])
    t_end = 6100
    i = 0
    while s.t < t_end:
        n = notes[i % 16]
        s.midi(0x90, n, 0, n, 60 + i % 60)
        if i % 8 == 7:
            s.midi(cc(1, i % 128), bend((i * 997) % 16384))
        i += 1
    s.midi(bend(8192), cc(1, 0), 0x80, [x for n in notes for x in (n, 0)])
    return s


def midisustain():
    s = Script("midisustain", "midisustain (R-MIDI-3): the sustain pedal. A note released under the\n"
               "pedal goes on until the pedal is up; one struck again under it\n"
               "starts again; a panel key (KEY1, note 53) and a MIDI note under\n"
               "the pedal; all notes off with the pedal down (the pedal still\n"
               "holds); the pedal up ends them all.")
    s.at(100).midi(cc(64, 127), on(60, 100)).wait(50).midi(off(60))
    s.wait(200).midi(on(60, 100)).wait(50).midi(off(60), on(64, 100))
    s.wait(100).event("key 14 down").wait(100).event("key 14 up").wait(10)
    s.midi(off(64)).wait(200).midi(cc(64, 0))
    s.wait(300).midi(on(67, 100), cc(64, 127), cc(123, 0)).wait(300).midi(cc(64, 0))
    return s


def midichan():
    s = Script("midichan", "midichan (R-MIDI-5): the channel test build receives on channel 10\n"
               "only: notes, controllers and program changes on every other channel\n"
               "are filtered; channel 10's play.")
    s.at(100)
    for ch in range(16):
        if ch != 9:
            s.midi(on(60 + ch, 100, ch), cc(7, 0, ch), [0xC0 | ch, 3], off(60 + ch, ch))
    s.wait(50).midi(on(72, 100, 9)).wait(200).midi(off(72, 9))
    return s


def midipanel():
    s = Script("midipanel", "midipanel (R-MIDI-6): MIDI and the panel together. KEY1 (note 53)\n"
               "and MIDI note 53 overlap, each released while the other holds; MIDI\n"
               "notes in the keyboard's range shown in cyan (screen at 900 ms, MIDI\n"
               "holding 60 and 64, KEY5 down); nothing left sounding.")
    s.at(100).event("key 14 down").wait(50).midi(on(53, 100)).wait(100).event("key 14 up")
    s.wait(100).midi(off(53))
    s.wait(100).midi(on(53, 100)).wait(50).event("key 14 down").wait(100).midi(off(53))
    s.wait(100).event("key 14 up")
    s.at(800).midi(on(60, 100), on(64, 100)).wait(5).event("key 18 down")
    s.at(1000).midi(off(60), off(64)).wait(5).event("key 18 up")
    return s


def midilat():
    s = Script("midilat", "midilat (R-MIDI-7): 20 notes, one every 150 ms, alone, so the time\n"
               "from each note on's last byte to its first sample can be measured.")
    s.at(100)
    for i in range(20):
        s.at(100 + 150 * i).midi(on(60 + i % 12, 100)).wait(60).midi(off(60 + i % 12))
    return s


CASES = (midimsg, midirun, midisysex, midijunk, mididense, midisustain, midichan, midipanel, midilat)


def stream(path):
    """The bytes of a script's `midi` events in order, and each byte's
    arrival time (ms)."""
    out = []
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            w = line.split("#")[0].split()
            if len(w) >= 3 and w[1] == "midi":
                t = float(w[0])
                for i, h in enumerate(w[2:]):
                    out.append((round(t + BYTE_MS * (i + 1), 3), int(h, 16)))
    return out


def main(argv):
    check = "--check" in argv
    bad = 0
    for case in CASES:
        s = case()
        path = os.path.join(SCRIPTS, s.name + ".txt")
        text = s.text()
        if check:
            old = open(path).read() if os.path.exists(path) else None
            if old != text:
                print("%s differs from what tools/midi_scripts.py writes" % path)
                bad = 1
        else:
            with open(path, "w") as f:
                f.write(text)
            print("wrote %s (%d lines, ends %.1f ms)" % (os.path.relpath(path, ROOT), len(s.lines), s.t))
    return bad


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

### 2026-10-23 M5: the FM engine
- Facts: HW-9 and HW-10 (releasing core 1, its state), HW-62 and HW-63
  (the float instructions, used per block only), HW-64 (the cores in
  fwtest), HW-65 (`testset` and `csync`, the SDK's lock and shared
  loads), HW-43 to HW-46 (the output), HW-36 and HW-39 (the panel's
  keys and knobs). PROVENANCE P-33 (the SDK's `cpu.h`, for the lock's
  syntax), P-34 (the literature below), P-35 (our experiments).
- Sources, all public literature, none of it code: John M. Chowning,
  "The Synthesis of Complex Audio Spectra by Means of Frequency
  Modulation", J. Audio Eng. Soc. 21(7), 1973 (a sine's phase modulated
  by another sine gives sidebands at fc ± n fm with amplitudes J_n(I));
  J. R. Carson's rule for an FM signal's bandwidth, about 2 (I + 1) fm
  (Proc. IRE, 1922); M. Abramowitz and I. Stegun, Handbook of
  Mathematical Functions (1964), 9.1.10, the Bessel functions' series
  (for the tests). Everything else is from first principles. No FM-1
  firmware, no other synthesizer's firmware and no FM engine's source was
  looked at; `vendor/` was left out of every search (it holds Plaits,
  which has an FM engine, and was not opened).

#### The operators

*Since M6a:* fwtest 0.3.0 runs all eight block-move modes (HW-66), so
`copy_words()` is gone and the copies are plain loops again. tools/build.sh
now fails an image holding the one gap left that the compiler emits, a
rotate by a register (docs/HARNESS.md, "Instructions", "Known gaps").

cat >> docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md <<'EOF'

### 2026-10-24 M6a: MIDI in
- Facts: none of the receiver's yet (SR-8, open when this was written);
  HARNESS.md's `midi` script event (a byte every 320 us). PROVENANCE P-38
  (what the spec and the SDK's header say so far), P-39 (the MIDI 1.0
  specification, as public literature).
- Sources: the MIDI 1.0 Detailed Specification's rules for status and
  data bytes, running status, realtime and System Exclusive messages, the
  channel mode messages (120 to 127), registered parameter 0 (pitch bend
  sensitivity) and the controller numbers' usual meanings, from the
  session's own knowledge; nothing fetched. No other synthesizer's
  firmware and no MIDI library's source was looked at.

#### The path
The receiver's interrupt only puts each byte into a 256-byte ring
(`midi_rx_byte`, midi.c). The engine's block callback, after the panel's
events, takes the bytes waiting, parses them and acts on each message
(`midi_read`, `midi_message` in fm_play.c), so MIDI and the panel change
the engine at one place and time, between blocks, and the voices never
change during one. At the wire's pace a block (1.45 ms) brings at most 5
bytes; the ring holds 256 (about 80 ms), so only a stalled engine could
fill it, and a full ring drops the newest bytes and counts them.

#### The parser
Our own, from the specification's rules (tools/midi_model.py is the same
rules written again in Python, for the tests):
- **Realtime** (0xF8 to 0xFF) is a message of its own wherever it comes,
  even between a status and its data or inside a SysEx, and changes
  nothing else. 0xF9 and 0xFD are undefined and dropped. 0xFF, a system
  reset, also ends running status and any SysEx, and the engine lets
  MIDI's notes go and its controllers back to rest.
- **Running status:** a channel status (0x80 to 0xEF) is kept for the
  data bytes that follow; every other status but realtime ends it.
- **System Exclusive** is skipped a byte at a time, so its length
  doesn't matter; past 4 096 data bytes it is counted as too long. EOX
  ends it; any other status (a note on, say) cuts it short and is taken
  as itself. Nothing in a SysEx is used yet.
- **Never wedged:** a data byte with no status, an undefined status, a
  stray EOX, and a message a status cuts short are dropped and counted.
  The parser's whole state is a status, two data bytes and a SysEx flag,
  so the next status byte always starts afresh.

#### Notes from two places
A note can be held by the panel's key, by MIDI and by the sustain pedal
at once, so each note keeps who holds it (`hold[]`, fm_play.c). A key
down from either sounds the note (again: the engine retriggers the voice
already playing it); a key up takes away only its own hold, and the
engine hears the note's off when no hold is left. So a MIDI note off
never ends a note the panel's key still holds, nor the reverse. While
the pedal is down, a released note passes to the pedal's hold, and the
pedal up ends every note it alone held. A note struck again under the
pedal starts again, and is the key's again.
- **All notes off** (CC 123, and 124 to 127) lets MIDI's keys go as
  their note offs would: notes the pedal holds go on until it is up.
- **All sound off** (CC 120) ends MIDI's and the pedal's notes and fades
  every voice out over the next block, as a stolen voice fades.
- **PRESETS, a program change and a mode change** release every voice,
  as in M5, and let the pedal's notes go; keys still down keep their
  hold, so their release later is an off the engine no longer needs.

#### The messages
- **Note on** with its velocity (1 to 127); a note on at velocity 0 is a
  note off; a note off's velocity is not used.
- **Pitch bend:** 14 bits, 8 192 the middle, +-the bend range, which is
  a setting (2 semitones by default) that registered parameter 0 (CC 101
  and 100 to 0, then CC 6) changes, up to 24. It moves every voice's
  pitch, phase-continuously, from the next block.
- **The modulation wheel** (CC 1) is vibrato: a 5.5 Hz sine on every
  voice's pitch, up to half a semitone at 127, stepped once a block.
- **Volume and expression** (CC 7, CC 11) scale the output after MASTER,
  each as its square; both start at 127, so without them nothing changes.
- **Program change** n selects test patch n (0 to 8), as PRESETS does;
  higher programs are ignored until M8's presets.
- **Mode messages:** 126 and 127 switch mono and poly, as SEL with MONO
  or POLY does; 124 and 125 (omni off and on) are only all notes off:
  the channel is the setting's.
- **Aftertouch** (channel and polyphonic) is parsed and not used.

#### The channel and the settings
`struct midi_settings` (midi.h) holds what MIDI uses: a version, the
receive channel (0: omni, the default; or 1 to 16), the bend range and
the controller map, all in bytes, so M7 can save it as it is and check
its version. Messages for another channel are counted and dropped; the
system messages are taken on every channel.

#### The controller map
A table of (controller, target) pairs in the settings, searched for each
controller change; the channel mode messages and the RPN controllers
(6, 100, 101) are fixed, as the specification has them. Default map:

| CC | Target |
|----|--------|
| 1 (modulation) | vibrato depth |
| 7 (volume), 11 (expression) | the output's level |
| 64 (damper) | the sustain pedal (down from 64) |
| 16 to 19 (general purpose 1 to 4) | KNOB1 to KNOB4 |
| 5 (portamento time) | KNOB2, the glide |
| 74 (brightness) | KNOB3, the modulators' level |

A knob's controller is an offset added to the panel's knob: 64 adds
nothing, 0 and 127 the ends of the knob's useful range (KNOB1 +-24
semitones, KNOB2 +-32 glide steps, KNOB3 -64 to +32 level steps, KNOB4
+-7 feedback steps), so the panel and MIDI can both move one. M8 adds
targets (and its macro controls) and MIDI learn by writing entries.

#### The screen
The keyboard on the panel screen shows the notes MIDI or the pedal holds
in cyan, at the keys that play them at the present octave (a key held on
the panel stays orange), and the event line shows each MIDI note as it
comes ("MIDI 1 note 60 on 100", "... off"). The engine posts each note to
a 16-entry queue main reads; a MIDI note before any panel event brings
up the panel screen, as a first event does.
EOF
echo ok

+  pitch, phase-continuously, from the next block.
+- **The modulation wheel** (CC 1) is vibrato: a 5.5 Hz sine on every
+  voice's pitch, up to half a semitone at 127, stepped once a block.
+- **Volume and expression** (CC 7, CC 11) scale the output after MASTER,
+  each as its square; both start at 127, so without them nothing changes.
+- **Program change** n selects test patch n (0 to 8), as PRESETS does;
+  higher programs are ignored until M8's presets.
+- **Mode messages:** 126 and 127 switch mono and poly, as SEL with MONO
+  or POLY does; 124 and 125 (omni off and on) are only all notes off:
+- **Aftertouch** (channel and polyphonic) is parsed and not used.
+`struct midi_settings` (midi.h) holds what MIDI uses: a version, the
+receive channel (0: omni, the default; or 1 to 16), the bend range and
+the controller map, all in bytes, so M7 can save it as it is and check
+its version. Messages for another channel are counted and dropped; the
+system messages are taken on every channel.
+A table of (controller, target) pairs in the settings, searched for each
+controller change; the channel mode messages and the RPN controllers
+(6, 100, 101) are fixed, as the specification has them. Default map:
+| 16 to 19 (general purpose 1 to 4) | KNOB1 to KNOB4 |
+A knob's controller is an offset added to the panel's knob: 64 adds
+nothing, 0 and 127 the ends of the knob's useful range (KNOB1 +-24
+semitones, KNOB2 +-32 glide steps, KNOB3 -64 to +32 level steps, KNOB4
++-7 feedback steps), so the panel and MIDI can both move one. M8 adds
+targets (and its macro controls) and MIDI learn by writing entries.
+The keyboard on the panel screen shows the notes MIDI or the pedal holds
+in cyan, at the keys that play them at the present octave (a key held on
+the panel stays orange), and the event line shows each MIDI note as it
+comes ("MIDI 1 note 60 on 100", "... off"). The engine posts each note to
+a 16-entry queue main reads; a MIDI note before any panel event brings
+up the panel screen, as a first event does.

content.text:
SR-8 hasn't been answered yet. Here's where M6a stands.

**Merged:** #74 (start), #75 (`copy_words` removed; the build check now catches the rotate by a register instead), and #76 (spec request SR-8). #76 went green before you merged it.

**Blocked on SR-8:** the spec doesn't yet say which UART and pin the MIDI jack uses, how to set up its receiver, its interrupt, or what fwtest counts as a receiver. Until it does, no MIDI byte can reach the firmware in fwtest, so none of the MIDI cases can run.

**Done meanwhile on `m6a/midi-in`** (pushed, no PR yet). The full suite still passes and the existing golden files are unchanged:
- **Parser:** our own. It handles running status and realtime bytes anywhere, skips SysEx of any length, and drops orphan, undefined and cut-short bytes, counting each so the tests can see them.
- **Note ownership:** each note remembers whether the panel key, MIDI or the sustain pedal holds it. So a MIDI note-off can't end a panel-held note, or the reverse.
- **Messages to the engine:** sustain, all notes off and all sound off, pitch bend with a settable range (2 semitones by default), mod wheel as vibrato, volume and expression, program change to test patches 0–8, and mono/poly mode switching.
- **Settings and CC map:** the receive channel (omni by default) sits in a settings struct M7 can save as it is. The CC map is a small table M8 can extend.
- **Display:** MIDI-held notes show in cyan on the screen's keyboard, and the event line shows each incoming note.
- **Tests:** a Python model of the parser, nine generated fwtest MIDI scripts, and 15 unit tests, all passing.

`git push` asked twice for an object this folder doesn't have. Both times, running `tools/clean-update.sh` from main fixed it, and its barrier check said "no spec-side files". I'll record this in EXPOSURE.

A background watch is running and will pick up the SR-8 answer when it lands. Then I'll write the receiver driver, run the MIDI cases and the latency measurement, and check the budgets.

-- Sources: the MIDI 1.0 Detailed Specification's rules for status and
-  data bytes, running status, realtime and System Exclusive messages, the
-  channel mode messages (120 to 127), registered parameter 0 (pitch bend
-  sensitivity) and the controller numbers' usual meanings, from the
-  session's own knowledge; nothing fetched. No other synthesizer's
-  firmware and no MIDI library's source was looked at.
-The receiver's interrupt only puts each byte into a 256-byte ring
-(`midi_rx_byte`, midi.c). The engine's block callback, after the panel's
-events, takes the bytes waiting, parses them and acts on each message
-(`midi_read`, `midi_message` in fm_play.c), so MIDI and the panel change
-the engine at one place and time, between blocks, and the voices never
-change during one. At the wire's pace a block (1.45 ms) brings at most 5
-bytes; the ring holds 256 (about 80 ms), so only a stalled engine could
-fill it, and a full ring drops the newest bytes and counts them.
-Our own, from the specification's rules (tools/midi_model.py is the same
-rules written again in Python, for the tests):
-- **Realtime** (0xF8 to 0xFF) is a message of its own wherever it comes,
-  even between a status and its data or inside a SysEx, and changes
-  nothing else. 0xF9 and 0xFD are undefined and dropped. 0xFF, a system
-  reset, also ends running status and any SysEx, and the engine lets
-  MIDI's notes go and its controllers back to rest.
-- **Running status:** a channel status (0x80 to 0xEF) is kept for the
-  data bytes that follow; every other status but realtime ends it.
-- **System Exclusive** is skipped a byte at a time, so its length
-  doesn't matter; past 4 096 data bytes it is counted as too long. EOX
-  ends it; any other status (a note on, say) cuts it short and is taken
-  as itself. Nothing in a SysEx is used yet.
-- **Never wedged:** a data byte with no status, an undefined status, a
-  stray EOX, and a message a status cuts short are dropped and counted.
-  The parser's whole state is a status, two data bytes and a SysEx flag,
-  so the next status byte always starts afresh.
-A note can be held by the panel's key, by MIDI and by the sustain pedal
-at once, so each note keeps who holds it (`hold[]`, fm_play.c). A key
-down from either sounds the note (again: the engine retriggers the voice
-already playing it); a key up takes away only its own hold, and the
-engine hears the note's off when no hold is left. So a MIDI note off
-never ends a note the panel's key still holds, nor the reverse. While
-the pedal is down, a released note passes to the pedal's hold, and the
-pedal up ends every note it alone held. A note struck again under the
-pedal starts again, and is the key's again.
-- **All notes off** (CC 123, and 124 to 127) lets MIDI's keys go as
-  their note offs would: notes the pedal holds go on until it is up.
-- **All sound off** (CC 120) ends MIDI's and the pedal's notes and fades
-  every voice out over the next block, as a stolen voice fades.
-- **PRESETS, a program change and a mode change** release every voice,
-  as in M5, and let the pedal's notes go; keys still down keep their
-  hold, so their release later is an off the engine no longer needs.
-- **Note on** with its velocity (1 to 127); a note on at velocity 0 is a
-  note off; a note off's velocity is not used.
-- **Pitch bend:** 14 bits, 8 192 the middle, +-the bend range, which is
-  a setting (2 semitones by default) that registered parameter 0 (CC 101
-  and 100 to 0, then CC 6) changes, up to 24. It moves every voice's
-  pitch, phase-continuously, from the next block.
-- **The modulation wheel** (CC 1) is vibrato: a 5.5 Hz sine on every

code='''# --- MIDI in (M6a; R-MIDI-*) ---------------------------------------------

MIDI_ADDR, MIDI_LEN = 0x01c005d0, 0x164
MIDI_FIELDS = ("marker", "bytes", "ring_dropped", "parsed", "messages", "realtime", "sysex",
               "sysex_bytes", "sysex_long", "sysex_cut", "orphans", "undefined", "cut", "filtered",
               "notes_on", "notes_off", "held", "pedal", "bend", "mod", "volume", "expression",
               "program", "last_note_tick", "log_count")
MIDI_MARKER = 0x3649444D      # "MDI6", firmware/src/midi.h
MIDI_LOG = 64
MIDI_LATENCY_MS = 3.0         # a note on's last byte to its first sample (R-MIDI-7)
MIDI_BEND_SEMI = 0.05         # a bent pitch, against the range asked
MIDI_LEVEL_DB = 0.1           # volume and expression against their curve
MIDI_SOUND_OFF_MS = 6.0       # all sound off: silent within this of its last byte


def midi_record(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        b = f.read()
    n = len(MIDI_FIELDS)
    r = dict(zip(MIDI_FIELDS, struct.unpack("<%dI" % n, b[:4 * n])))
    r["bend"] = struct.unpack("<i", struct.pack("<I", r["bend"]))[0]
    r["log"] = [tuple(b[4 * n + 4 * i:4 * n + 4 * i + 4]) for i in range(MIDI_LOG)]
    return r


def midi_name(when="end"):
    return "ram-%08x-%x-%s.bin" % (MIDI_ADDR, MIDI_LEN, when)


def midi_logged(r):
    """The messages still in the record's log, oldest first."""
    n = r["log_count"]
    return [r["log"][i % MIDI_LOG] for i in range(max(0, n - MIDI_LOG), n)]


def midi_notes(model, channel=None):
    """(note ons, note offs) the engine should take from the model's log."""
    on = off = 0
    for s, d1, d2, _ in model.log:
        if s >= 0xF0 or (channel is not None and s & 15 != channel):
            continue
        if s & 0xF0 == 0x90 and d2:
            on += 1
        elif s & 0xF0 in (0x80, 0x90):
            off += 1
    return on, off


def midi_common(name, case_dir, idle=True, channel=None):
    """Every MIDI case: fwtest dropped no byte; the firmware received and
    parsed every byte of the script, and its counters and its log of
    messages are the model's (tools/midi_model.py) for the same bytes; it
    took the note ons and offs the model's messages hold; and, if idle,
    nothing is held and no voice sounds at the end."""
    problems, lines = [], []
    with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "result.json")) as f:
        run = json.load(f).get("run", {})
    if run.get("midi_bytes_dropped"):
        problems.append("%s: fwtest dropped %s MIDI bytes" % (name, run["midi_bytes_dropped"]))
    stream = [b for _, b in midi_scripts.stream(os.path.join(ROOT, "tests", "fw", "scripts", name + ".txt"))]
    model = midi_model.parse(stream)
    r = midi_record(os.path.join(case_dir, midi_name()))
    if r["marker"] != MIDI_MARKER:
        return problems + ["%s: the MIDI record's marker is 0x%08x" % (name, r["marker"])], lines, r, model
    if (r["bytes"], r["ring_dropped"], r["parsed"]) != (len(stream), 0, len(stream)):
        problems.append("%s: %d bytes received, %d dropped, %d parsed; the script sends %d"
                        % (name, r["bytes"], r["ring_dropped"], r["parsed"], len(stream)))
    for k in midi_model.COUNTERS:
        if r[k] != model.count[k]:
            problems.append("%s: %s %d, the model says %d" % (name, k, r[k], model.count[k]))
    if r["log_count"] != len(model.log):
        problems.append("%s: %d messages logged, the model has %d" % (name, r["log_count"], len(model.log)))
    elif midi_logged(r) != model.log[-MIDI_LOG:]:
        problems.append("%s: the logged messages differ from the model's" % name)
    on, off = midi_notes(model, channel)
    if (r["notes_on"], r["notes_off"]) != (on, off):
        problems.append("%s: %d note ons and %d offs taken, expected %d and %d"
                        % (name, r["notes_on"], r["notes_off"], on, off))
    f = fm_record(os.path.join(case_dir, fm_name()))
    if idle and (r["held"] or r["pedal"] or f["voices0"] or f["voices1"]):
        problems.append("%s: at the end %d notes held, pedal %d, %d + %d voices sounding: a stuck note"
                        % (name, r["held"], r["pedal"], f["voices0"], f["voices1"]))
    lines.append("  midi: %d bytes, %d messages (%d realtime), %d SysEx (%d bytes, %d too long, %d cut), "
                 "%d orphans, %d undefined, %d cut, %d filtered; %d note ons, %d offs; model: same"
                 % (r["bytes"], r["messages"], r["realtime"], r["sysex"], r["sysex_bytes"], r["sysex_long"],
                    r["sysex_cut"], r["orphans"], r["undefined"], r["cut"], r["filtered"],
                    r["notes_on"], r["notes_off"]) if not problems else
                 "  midi: %d bytes, %d messages" % (r["bytes"], r["messages"]))
    return problems, lines, r, model


def midi_times(name, status, d1=None):
    """Arrival times (ms) of the last byte of each message in a script
    whose status (high nibble for channel messages) and first data byte
    match, running status included."""
    out, cur, have = [], 0, []
    for t, b in midi_scripts.stream(os.path.join(ROOT, "tests", "fw", "scripts", name + ".txt")):
        if b >= 0xF8:
            continue
        if b >= 0x80:
            cur, have = (b if b < 0xF0 else 0), []
            continue
        if not cur:
            continue
        have.append(b)
        if len(have) == midi_model.data_bytes(cur):
            if (cur & 0xF0) == status and (d1 is None or have[0] == d1):
                out.append((t, have))
            have = []
    return out


def pitch_at(x, ends, t0, t1):
    """The median pitch (MIDI note) of the sound between t0 and t1 ms."""
    first = next(i for i in range(len(x)) if aa.sample_ms(i, ends) >= t0)
    last = next(i for i in range(first, len(x)) if aa.sample_ms(i, ends) >= t1)
    track = sorted(69 + 12 * math.log2(hz / 440.0) for _, hz in aa.pitch_track(x, first, last))
    return track[len(track) // 2] if track else None, track


def level_at(x, ends, t0, t1):
    at = lambda ms: next(i for i in range(len(x)) if aa.sample_ms(i, ends) >= ms)
    return rms_db(x[at(t0):at(t1)])


def check_midimsg(case_dir):
    """Every message the engine takes (R-MIDI-2, R-MIDI-3): the bends at
    the default range and after RPN 0 sets 12, the mod wheel's vibrato,
    volume and expression, all sound off, the program change."""
    problems, lines, a, _, wav = check_audio_common("midimsg", case_dir)
    more, l2, r, _ = midi_common("midimsg", case_dir)
    problems, lines = problems + more, lines + l2
    f = fm_record(os.path.join(case_dir, fm_name()))
    if r["program"] != 8 or f["patch"] != 8:
        problems.append("midimsg: program %d, patch %d in force; expected 8 (9 is ignored)" % (r["program"], f["patch"]))
    if (r["bend"], r["mod"], r["volume"], r["expression"]) != (0, 0, 127, 127):
        problems.append("midimsg: at the end bend %d, mod %d, volume %d, expression %d"
                        % (r["bend"], r["mod"], r["volume"], r["expression"]))
    if wav is None:
        return problems + ["midimsg: no audio.wav"], lines
    x, ends = wav
    bends = midi_times("midimsg", 0xE0)
    ccs = {(d[0], d[1]): t for t, d in midi_times("midimsg", 0xB0)}
    # Note 64 bent to the top (+2), and note 65 at range 12 (+12).
    want = []
    for t, d in bends:
        if d == [0x7F, 0x7F]:
            nxt = min(u for u, _ in bends if u > t)
            want.append((t, nxt))
    got = []
    for (t0, t1), note in zip(want, (66, 77)):
        p, _ = pitch_at(x, ends, t0 + 5, t1 - 2)
        got.append(p)
        if p is None or abs(p - note) > MIDI_BEND_SEMI:
            problems.append("midimsg: bent to the top, note %s, not %d" % (p, note))
    # Vibrato: CC 1 at 127 swings note 64 by half a semitone.
    _, track = pitch_at(x, ends, ccs[(1, 127)] + 20, ccs[(1, 0)] - 5)
    swing = (track[-1] - track[0]) / 2 if track else 0
    if not 0.4 <= swing <= 0.55:
        problems.append("midimsg: vibrato swings %.3f semitones, not about 0.5" % swing)
    # Volume 64 and expression 100: (64/127)^2 (100/127)^2 against note 60's level.
    ons = midi_times("midimsg", 0x90)
    t60 = ons[0][0]
    t67 = next(t for t, d in ons if d[0] == 67)
    ref, low = level_at(x, ends, t60 + 30, t60 + 120), level_at(x, ends, t67 + 30, t67 + 90)
    expect = 40 * math.log10(64 / 127.0) + 40 * math.log10(100 / 127.0)
    if abs((low - ref) - expect) > MIDI_LEVEL_DB:
        problems.append("midimsg: volume and expression take %.2f dB, not %.2f" % (low - ref, expect))
    # All sound off: silent soon after its last byte.
    t_off = ccs[(120, 0)]
    after = [i for i in range(len(x)) if t_off + MIDI_SOUND_OFF_MS <= aa.sample_ms(i, ends) < t_off + 50]
    loud = max(abs(x[i]) for i in after) if after else 0
    if loud:
        problems.append("midimsg: still sounding %.1f ms after all sound off (peak %d)" % (MIDI_SOUND_OFF_MS, loud))
    lines.append("  bent to notes %s (66, 77 asked); vibrato +-%.3f semitones; volume and expression %.2f dB "
                 "(%.2f); silent %.0f ms after all sound off; program 8 in force"
                 % (", ".join("%.3f" % g for g in got if g is not None), swing, low - ref, expect, MIDI_SOUND_OFF_MS))
    return problems, lines


def midi_only(name):
    def check(case_dir):
        problems, lines, a, _, _ = check_audio_common(name, case_dir)
        more, l2, r, model = midi_common(name, case_dir)
        return problems + more, lines + l2
    return check


def check_mididense(case_dir):
    """The wire full for 6 s (R-MIDI-4): every byte taken, every note on
    and off, no underrun, all 16 voices used, nothing stuck at the end."""
    problems, lines, a, _, _ = check_audio_common("mididense", case_dir)
    more, l2, r, model = midi_common("mididense", case_dir)
    f = fm_record(os.path.join(case_dir, fm_name()))
    if f["voices_max"] != FM_VOICES:
        more.append("mididense: at most %d voices at once, not %d" % (f["voices_max"], FM_VOICES))
    lines = lines + l2 + ["  %d voices at most; %d notes started; longest fill %.1f us"
                          % (f["voices_max"], f["notes"], a["fill_max"] / 24.0)]
    return problems + more, lines


# midisustain's captures: (ms, notes MIDI or the pedal holds, pedal down).
SUSTAIN_AT = ((300, 1, 1), (560, 2, 1), (700, 3, 1), (1000, 0, 0), (1300, 1, 1))


def check_midisustain(case_dir):
    """The sustain pedal (R-MIDI-3): a note released under it held on, a
    note struck again under it, a panel key released under it, all notes
    off with it down; the pedal up ends them."""
    problems, lines, a, _, _ = check_audio_common("midisustain", case_dir)
    more, l2, r, _ = midi_common("midisustain", case_dir)
    problems, lines = problems + more, lines + l2
    seen = []
    for ms, held, pedal in SUSTAIN_AT:
        c = midi_record(os.path.join(case_dir, midi_name("%dms" % ms)))
        f = fm_record(os.path.join(case_dir, fm_name("%dms" % ms)))
        on = f["voices0"] + f["voices1"]
        seen.append("%d ms: %d held, pedal %d, %d sounding" % (ms, c["held"], c["pedal"], on))
        if (c["held"], c["pedal"]) != (held, pedal) or (held and on < held):
            problems.append("midisustain: at %d ms %d held, pedal %d, %d voices sounding; expected %d, %d"
                            % (ms, c["held"], c["pedal"], on, held, pedal))
    lines.append("  " + "; ".join(seen))
    return problems, lines


def check_midichan(case_dir):
    """The channel test build, on channel 10 (R-MIDI-5): everything on the
    other 15 channels filtered, channel 10's note played."""
    problems, lines, a, _, _ = check_audio_common("midichan", case_dir)
    more, l2, r, model = midi_common("midichan", case_dir, channel=9)
    problems, lines = problems + more, lines + l2
    others = sum(1 for s, _, _, _ in model.log if s < 0xF0 and s & 15 != 9)
    if r["filtered"] != others:
        problems.append("midichan: %d messages filtered, %d were for other channels" % (r["filtered"], others))
    if r["volume"] != 127 or r["program"] != 0xFFFFFFFF or r["notes_on"] != 1:
        problems.append("midichan: volume %d, program 0x%x, %d note ons: another channel got through"
                        % (r["volume"], r["program"], r["notes_on"]))
    return problems, lines


# midipanel's captures: (ms, voices sounding at least).
PANEL_AT = ((200, 1), (300, 1), (500, 1), (600, 1), (900, 3))


def check_midipanel(case_dir):
    """MIDI and the panel together (R-MIDI-6): the same note held from
    both, each released while the other holds it, sounds on; the screen
    (golden) shows MIDI's notes; nothing stuck at the end."""
    problems, lines, a, _, _ = check_audio_common("midipanel", case_dir)
    more, l2, r, _ = midi_common("midipanel", case_dir)
    problems, lines = problems + more, lines + l2
    seen = []
    for ms, voices in PANEL_AT:
        f = fm_record(os.path.join(case_dir, fm_name("%dms" % ms)))
        on = f["voices0"] + f["voices1"]
        seen.append("%d ms: %d" % (ms, on))
        if on < voices:
            problems.append("midipanel: at %d ms %d voices sound, expected at least %d" % (ms, on, voices))
    lines.append("  voices sounding at " + ", ".join(seen))
    return problems, lines


def check_midilat(case_dir):
    """Latency (R-MIDI-7): from each note on's last byte (the script's time
    and the wire's pace, docs/HARNESS.md) to the first sample of its sound
    (ipb.csv's block ends, exact), within MIDI_LATENCY_MS."""
    problems, lines, a, _, wav = check_audio_common("midilat", case_dir)
    more, l2, r, _ = midi_common("midilat", case_dir)
    problems, lines = problems + more, lines + l2
    if wav is None:
        return problems + ["midilat: no audio.wav"], lines
    x, ends = wav
    starts = [aa.sample_ms(first, ends) for first, _ in sounds(x)]
    ons = [t for t, d in midi_times("midilat", 0x90) if d[1]]
    lat = []
    for t in ons:
        s = [u for u in starts if u >= t]
        lat.append(s[0] - t if s else None)
    if len(starts) != len(ons) or None in lat:
        return problems + ["midilat: %d sounds for %d note ons" % (len(starts), len(ons))], lines
    lines.append("  latency, last byte to first sample: %.3f to %.3f ms, mean %.3f (bound %.1f), %d notes"
                 % (min(lat), max(lat), sum(lat) / len(lat), MIDI_LATENCY_MS, len(lat)))
    if max(lat) > MIDI_LATENCY_MS or min(lat) < 0:
        problems.append("midilat: latency %.3f to %.3f ms, bound %.1f" % (min(lat), max(lat), MIDI_LATENCY_MS))
    return problems, lines


MIDI_CHECKS = {"midimsg": check_midimsg, "midirun": midi_only("midirun"),
               "midisysex": midi_only("midisysex"), "midijunk": midi_only("midijunk"),
               "mididense": check_mididense, "midisustain": check_midisustain,
               "midichan": check_midichan, "midipanel": check_midipanel, "midilat": check_midilat}


'''

t=t.replace(anchor, code+anchor)
t=t.replace('''"fmsteal": check_fmsteal, "fmvel": check_fmvel, "fmgold": check_fmgold, "fmgold2": check_fmgold}''','''"fmsteal": check_fmsteal, "fmvel": check_fmvel, "fmgold": check_fmgold, "fmgold2": check_fmgold}
AUDIO_CHECKS.update(MIDI_CHECKS)''')
open(p,'w').write(t)

def midi_times(name, status, d1=None):
    """Arrival times (ms) of the last byte of each message in a script
    whose status (high nibble for channel messages) and first data byte
    match, running status included."""
    out, cur, have = [], 0, []
    for t, b in midi_scripts.stream(os.path.join(ROOT, "tests", "fw", "scripts", name + ".txt")):
        if b >= 0xF8:
            continue
        if b >= 0x80:
            cur, have = (b if b < 0xF0 else 0), []
            continue
        if not cur:
            continue
        have.append(b)
        if len(have) == midi_model.data_bytes(cur):
            if (cur & 0xF0) == status and (d1 is None or have[0] == d1):
                out.append((t, have))
            have = []
    return out


def pitch_at(x, ends, t0, t1):
    """The median pitch (MIDI note) of the sound between t0 and t1 ms."""
    first = next(i for i in range(len(x)) if aa.sample_ms(i, ends) >= t0)
    last = next(i for i in range(first, len(x)) if aa.sample_ms(i, ends) >= t1)
    track = sorted(69 + 12 * math.log2(hz / 440.0) for _, hz in aa.pitch_track(x, first, last))
    return track[len(track) // 2] if track else None, track


def level_at(x, ends, t0, t1):
    at = lambda ms: next(i for i in range(len(x)) if aa.sample_ms(i, ends) >= ms)
    return rms_db(x[at(t0):at(t1)])


def check_midimsg(case_dir):
    """Every message the engine takes (R-MIDI-2, R-MIDI-3): the bends at
    the default range and after RPN 0 sets 12, the mod wheel's vibrato,
    volume and expression, all sound off, the program change."""
    problems, lines, a, _, wav = check_audio_common("midimsg", case_dir)
    more, l2, r, _ = midi_common("midimsg", case_dir)
    problems, lines = problems + more, lines + l2
    f = fm_record(os.path.join(case_dir, fm_name()))
    if r["program"] != 8 or f["patch"] != 8:
        problems.append("midimsg: program %d, patch %d in force; expected 8 (9 is ignored)" % (r["program"], f["patch"]))
    if (r["bend"], r["mod"], r["volume"], r["expression"]) != (0, 0, 127, 127):
        problems.append("midimsg: at the end bend %d, mod %d, volume %d, expression %d"
                        % (r["bend"], r["mod"], r["volume"], r["expression"]))
    if wav is None:
        return problems + ["midimsg: no audio.wav"], lines
    x, ends = wav
    bends = midi_times("midimsg", 0xE0)
    ccs = {(d[0], d[1]): t for t, d in midi_times("midimsg", 0xB0)}
    # Note 64 bent to the top (+2), and note 65 at range 12 (+12).
    want = []
    for t, d in bends:
        if d == [0x7F, 0x7F]:
            nxt = min(u for u, _ in bends if u > t)
            want.append((t, nxt))
    got = []
    for (t0, t1), note in zip(want, (66, 77)):
        p, _ = pitch_at(x, ends, t0 + 5, t1 - 2)
        got.append(p)
        if p is None or abs(p - note) > MIDI_BEND_SEMI:
            problems.append("midimsg: bent to the top, note %s, not %d" % (p, note))
    # Vibrato: CC 1 at 127 swings note 64 by half a semitone.
    _, track = pitch_at(x, ends, ccs[(1, 127)] + 20, ccs[(1, 0)] - 5)
    swing = (track[-1] - track[0]) / 2 if track else 0
    if not 0.4 <= swing <= 0.55:
        problems.append("midimsg: vibrato swings %.3f semitones, not about 0.5" % swing)
    # Volume 64 and expression 100: (64/127)^2 (100/127)^2 against note 60's level.
    ons = midi_times("midimsg", 0x90)
    t60 = ons[0][0]
    t67 = next(t for t, d in ons if d[0] == 67)
    ref, low = level_at(x, ends, t60 + 30, t60 + 120), level_at(x, ends, t67 + 30, t67 + 90)
    expect = 40 * math.log10(64 / 127.0) + 40 * math.log10(100 / 127.0)
    if abs((low - ref) - expect) > MIDI_LEVEL_DB:
        problems.append("midimsg: volume and expression take %.2f dB, not %.2f" % (low - ref, expect))
    # All sound off: silent soon after its last byte.
    t_off = ccs[(120, 0)]
    after = [i for i in range(len(x)) if t_off + MIDI_SOUND_OFF_MS <= aa.sample_ms(i, ends) < t_off + 50]
    loud = max(abs(x[i]) for i in after) if after else 0
    if loud:
        problems.append("midimsg: still sounding %.1f ms after all sound off (peak %d)" % (MIDI_SOUND_OFF_MS, loud))
    lines.append("  bent to notes %s (66, 77 asked); vibrato +-%.3f semitones; volume and expression %.2f dB "
                 "(%.2f); silent %.0f ms after all sound off; program 8 in force"
                 % (", ".join("%.3f" % g for g in got if g is not None), swing, low - ref, expect, MIDI_SOUND_OFF_MS))
    return problems, lines


def midi_only(name):
    def check(case_dir):
        problems, lines, a, _, _ = check_audio_common(name, case_dir)
        more, l2, r, model = midi_common(name, case_dir)
        return problems + more, lines + l2
    return check


def check_mididense(case_dir):
    """The wire full for 6 s (R-MIDI-4): every byte taken, every note on
    and off, no underrun, all 16 voices used, nothing stuck at the end."""
    problems, lines, a, _, _ = check_audio_common("mididense", case_dir)
    more, l2, r, model = midi_common("mididense", case_dir)
    f = fm_record(os.path.join(case_dir, fm_name()))
    if f["voices_max"] != FM_VOICES:
        more.append("mididense: at most %d voices at once, not %d" % (f["voices_max"], FM_VOICES))
    lines = lines + l2 + ["  %d voices at most; %d notes started; longest fill %.1f us"
                          % (f["voices_max"], f["notes"], a["fill_max"] / 24.0)]
    return problems + more, lines

SUSTAIN_AT = ((300, 1, 1), (560, 2, 1), (700, 3, 1), (1000, 0, 0), (1300, 1, 1))


def check_midisustain(case_dir):
    """The sustain pedal (R-MIDI-3): a note released under it held on, a
    note struck again under it, a panel key released under it, all notes
    off with it down; the pedal up ends them."""
    problems, lines, a, _, _ = check_audio_common("midisustain", case_dir)
    more, l2, r, _ = midi_common("midisustain", case_dir)
    problems, lines = problems + more, lines + l2
    seen = []
    for ms, held, pedal in SUSTAIN_AT:
        c = midi_record(os.path.join(case_dir, midi_name("%dms" % ms)))
        f = fm_record(os.path.join(case_dir, fm_name("%dms" % ms)))
        on = f["voices0"] + f["voices1"]
        seen.append("%d ms: %d held, pedal %d, %d sounding" % (ms, c["held"], c["pedal"], on))
        if (c["held"], c["pedal"]) != (held, pedal) or (held and on < held):
            problems.append("midisustain: at %d ms %d held, pedal %d, %d voices sounding; expected %d, %d"
                            % (ms, c["held"], c["pedal"], on, held, pedal))
    lines.append("  " + "; ".join(seen))
    return problems, lines


def check_midichan(case_dir):
    """The channel test build, on channel 10 (R-MIDI-5): everything on the
    other 15 channels filtered, channel 10's note played."""
    problems, lines, a, _, _ = check_audio_common("midichan", case_dir)
    more, l2, r, model = midi_common("midichan", case_dir, channel=9)
    problems, lines = problems + more, lines + l2
    others = sum(1 for s, _, _, _ in model.log if s < 0xF0 and s & 15 != 9)
    if r["filtered"] != others:
        problems.append("midichan: %d messages filtered, %d were for other channels" % (r["filtered"], others))
    if r["volume"] != 127 or r["program"] != 0xFFFFFFFF or r["notes_on"] != 1:
        problems.append("midichan: volume %d, program 0x%x, %d note ons: another channel got through"
                        % (r["volume"], r["program"], r["notes_on"]))
    return problems, lines


# midipanel's captures: (ms, voices sounding at least).
PANEL_AT = ((200, 1), (300, 1), (500, 1), (600, 1), (900, 3))


def check_midipanel(case_dir):
    """MIDI and the panel together (R-MIDI-6): the same note held from
    both, each released while the other holds it, sounds on; the screen
    (golden) shows MIDI's notes; nothing stuck at the end."""
    problems, lines, a, _, _ = check_audio_common("midipanel", case_dir)
    more, l2, r, _ = midi_common("midipanel", case_dir)
    problems, lines = problems + more, lines + l2
    seen = []
    for ms, voices in PANEL_AT:
        f = fm_record(os.path.join(case_dir, fm_name("%dms" % ms)))
        on = f["voices0"] + f["voices1"]
        seen.append("%d ms: %d" % (ms, on))
        if on < voices:
            problems.append("midipanel: at %d ms %d voices sound, expected at least %d" % (ms, on, voices))
    lines.append("  voices sounding at " + ", ".join(seen))
    return problems, lines


def check_midilat(case_dir):
    """Latency (R-MIDI-7): from each note on's last byte (the script's time
    and the wire's pace, docs/HARNESS.md) to the first sample of its sound
    (ipb.csv's block ends, exact), within MIDI_LATENCY_MS."""
    problems, lines, a, _, wav = check_audio_common("midilat", case_dir)
    more, l2, r, _ = midi_common("midilat", case_dir)
    problems, lines = problems + more, lines + l2
    if wav is None:
        return problems + ["midilat: no audio.wav"], lines
    x, ends = wav
    starts = [aa.sample_ms(first, ends) for first, _ in sounds(x)]
    ons = [t for t, d in midi_times("midilat", 0x90) if d[1]]
    lat = []
    for t in ons:
        s = [u for u in starts if u >= t]
        lat.append(s[0] - t if s else None)

        return problems + ["midilat: %d sounds for %d note ons" % (len(starts), len(ons))], lines
    lines.append("  latency, last byte to first sample: %.3f to %.3f ms, mean %.3f (bound %.1f), %d notes"

    return problems, lines

p='docs/REQUIREMENTS.md'; t=open(p).read()
anchor='| R-AUDIT-1 |'
rows='''| R-MIDI-1 | MIDI in's parser (M6a; firmware/src/midi.c): our own MIDI 1.0 byte parser with running status; realtime bytes (0xF8 to 0xFF) taken anywhere, inside other messages and SysEx too, without disturbing them; System Exclusive skipped whatever its length (past 4 096 data bytes counted as too long) and ended by EOX or cut short by any other status; orphan data bytes, undefined status bytes, stray EOX and messages a status cuts short dropped and counted, so no input wedges it. In fwtest the firmware receives and parses every byte of each MIDI script, and its counters and its log of messages equal those of an independent model of the same rules (tools/midi_model.py) for the same bytes: running status with realtime interleaved, a SysEx flood (short ones, one of 6 000 bytes, one cut short, realtime inside, a stray EOX), truncated messages and 3 000 random bytes, each followed by notes that play. | M6a | C-FW-SUITE, C-UNIT |
| R-MIDI-2 | MIDI's messages to the engine: note on with velocity (velocity 0 a note off), note off, pitch bend (14 bits, +-the bend range, 2 semitones by default, set by RPN 0 up to 24), the modulation wheel (vibrato, 5.5 Hz, up to half a semitone), volume and expression (each as its square, after MASTER), program change (test patch n for n < 9; others ignored), all notes off, all sound off, reset all controllers, mono and poly on, system reset; aftertouch parsed and not used. In fwtest: a bend to the top is +2 semitones, and +12 after RPN 0 sets 12, within 0.05; the vibrato swings 0.4 to 0.55 semitones; volume 64 and expression 100 take their curve's level within 0.1 dB; all sound off is silent within 6 ms of its last byte; the program change selects test patch 8 and ignores 9. | M6a | C-FW-SUITE |
| R-MIDI-3 | Holding notes: each note keeps who holds it (the panel's key, MIDI, the sustain pedal, CC 64); the engine hears its off only when nothing holds it. A note released while the pedal is down goes on until the pedal is up; one struck again under it starts again; a panel key released under it is held too; all notes off with the pedal down leaves the pedal's notes held until it is up. In fwtest the notes held and the pedal at five times through such a script are what these rules give, and nothing is held or sounding at the end. | M6a | C-FW-SUITE |
| R-MIDI-4 | A dense stream: the wire full for 6 s (16 notes held, each struck again in turn in running status, the mod wheel and pitch bend moving between): every byte received and parsed, every note on and off taken, all 16 voices used, no underrun, and nothing held or sounding after the notes off. | M6a | C-FW-SUITE, C-UNIT |
| R-MIDI-5 | The receive channel: a setting (omni by default, or 1 to 16) in `struct midi_settings` (midi.h), with the bend range and the controller map, all bytes and versioned so M7 can save it as it is. Channel messages for another channel are dropped and counted. The channel test build (channel 10): notes, controllers and program changes on the other 15 channels have no effect, and channel 10's note plays. | M6a | C-FW-SUITE |
| R-MIDI-6 | MIDI and the panel together: the same note held from both, each released while the other holds it, sounds on, and nothing is left sounding; the panel screen shows the notes MIDI or the pedal holds in cyan at the keys that play them, and each MIDI note on the event line (golden image). The controller map (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M6a) is a table in the settings: CC 1 vibrato, 7 volume, 11 expression, 64 the pedal, 16 to 19 KNOB1 to KNOB4, 5 the glide (KNOB2), 74 the modulators' level (KNOB3), each knob's controller an offset to the panel's knob. | M6a | C-FW-SUITE; review |
| R-MIDI-7 | Latency: from a note on's last byte to the first sample of its sound, timed by the script's time, the wire's pace and fwtest's block end times (docs/HARNESS.md), at most 3.0 ms for each of 20 notes. | M6a | C-FW-SUITE |
'''
assert t.count(anchor)==1
t=t.replace(anchor, rows+anchor)
open(p,'w').write(t)
p='tools/record.py'; t=open(p).read()
old='''              "R-FM-1", "R-FM-3", "R-FM-4", "R-FM-5", "R-FM-6", "R-FM-8", "R-FM-9"],
     "cmd": lambda: [PY, "-I", "tools/fw-suite.py",'''
assert t.count(old)==1
t=t.replace(old,'''              "R-FM-1", "R-FM-3", "R-FM-4", "R-FM-5", "R-FM-6", "R-FM-8", "R-FM-9",
              "R-MIDI-1", "R-MIDI-2", "R-MIDI-3", "R-MIDI-4", "R-MIDI-5", "R-MIDI-6", "R-MIDI-7"],
     "cmd": lambda: [PY, "-I", "tools/fw-suite.py",''')
open(p,'w').write(t)
EOF
sed -n 70,80p tools/record.py

content.content:
## 16. MIDI input (SR-8)

### HW-67: The FM-1's MIDI inputs, and the one fwtest feeds
- Fact: The FM-1 takes MIDI in three ways, all active at once: a 3.5 mm
  MIDI IN jack carrying serial MIDI at 31 250 baud, USB MIDI (the FM-1 is a
  class-compliant USB device with a MIDI and an audio interface), and MIDI
  over Bluetooth LE. Its manual lists no MIDI OUT jack. On the chip, the
  jack's serial MIDI is received by UART1 (`JL_UART1`, HW-68), through its
  receive DMA. fwtest models only the jack:
  a script's `midi` event (HARNESS, "Input scripts") delivers its bytes to
  UART1's receiver, and fwtest has no USB or Bluetooth MIDI. Which pin the
  jack reaches, and how the TRS socket is wired (type A or B), the sources
  don't say (Q-12).
- Sources: MAN (the FM-1's manual, English part, p. 10, "MIDI
  Connectivity": the three interfaces, the jack's 31 250 baud; "What the
  FM-1 sends via MIDI"); RE `docs/io/05-midi.md` §1 and §2 (the three
  transports; UART MIDI on the UART at `0x00012100`, received by DMA),
  `docs/io/06-usb.md` §1 (a USB composite device, audio and MIDI),
  `docs/reversing/01-hardware-map.md` (MIDI I/O: USB and UART MIDI); SDK
  `WL82.h` lines 569-591 (UART1's base); E-19 (fwtest's `midi` bytes reach
  UART1's ring).
- Standing: confirmed (MAN, RE, SDK, E-19)
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-68: The UARTs' registers, sources, pins and clocks
- Fact: The chip has three UARTs, `JL_UART0`, `JL_UART1` and `JL_UART2`,
  at `0x00012000`, `0x00012100` and `0x00012200`. Each has the words, from
  its base: `CON0` +0x00, `CON1` +0x04, `BAUD` +0x08, `BUF` +0x0C, `OTCNT`
  +0x10, `TXADR` +0x14, `TXCNT` +0x18, `RXSADR` +0x1C, `RXEADR` +0x20,
  `RXCNT` +0x24, `HRXCNT` +0x28. `CON0`, `CON1`, `BAUD`, `TXCNT` and
  `HRXCNT` are 16 bits and `BUF` 8 bits, each in the low part of its word;
  `BAUD` and `TXCNT` are write-only and `HRXCNT` read-only. Their interrupt
  sources are 19, 20 and 21. A UART's transmit and receive pins are either
  one of its fixed pin pairs, given as transmit then receive (UART1: PH6 and
  PH7, PC3 and PC4, PB3 and PB4, or the USB pins), or any pin, through an
  output and an input channel of the port map (`JL_IOMAP`). The UART clock
  is the low-speed bus clock, the crystal oscillator or the PLL's 48 MHz
  (`CLK_CON1` bits 10-11, HW-53). The SDK's driver receives into a circular
  buffer by DMA, with an interrupt after a given number of bytes and an
  idle timeout counted in clocks, and each of the transmit, receive and
  timeout interrupts can be left off. The SDK gives no bit meanings for
  `CON0`, `CON1` or `BAUD` (its UART driver is a prebuilt library).
- Sources: SDK `WL82.h` lines 12-16 (the bases, `map_adr`) and 569-591
  (`JL_UART_TypeDef`, the three bases); SDK
  `include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/hwi.h` lines 59-61 (sources 19 to 21);
  SDK `include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/uart.h` (three UARTs, the pin pairs,
  the input and output channels); SDK `include_lib/driver/device/uart.h`
  (the clock choices, the circular buffer, the byte count and idle timeout,
  the interrupts that can be left off).
- Standing: confirmed (SDK)
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-69: UART1's receive flags, their acknowledge and the count latch
- Fact: In UART1's `CON0`, read: bit 14 is set when the receive DMA has
  taken the set number of bytes (receive pending), bit 11 when the line has
  been idle for the set time after a byte (timeout pending). Written as 1:
  bit 12 clears the receive pending, bit 10 the timeout pending, bit 13 the
  transmit pending; bit 7 latches into `HRXCNT` how many bytes the receive
  DMA has written since the previous latch, and `HRXCNT` keeps that count
  until the next latch. FM-1's own firmware receives MIDI from the jack
  this way, by DMA, on source 20.
- Sources: RE `docs/io/05-midi.md` §2.1 (the UART's flags at `0x00012100`:
  `0x4000` receive pending, `0x800` timeout; acknowledged with `0x80`,
  `0x1000`, `0x400`, `0x2000`; the count at `0x00012128` read in the
  handler); E-19 (the same bits in fwtest).
- Standing: confirmed (RE, E-19)
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-70: UART1's receive set-up bits, the ring, the count and the timeout
- Fact: In UART1's `CON0`: bit 0 turns the UART on; bit 2 enables the
  transmit interrupt, bit 3 the receive interrupt (bit 14, HW-69), bit 5
  the timeout interrupt (bit 11); bit 6 turns the receive DMA on. The DMA
  writes each byte at the next address of the ring from `RXSADR` up to,
  not including, `RXEADR`, and wraps to `RXSADR`; writing `RXSADR` starts
  it again at the ring's start. `RXCNT` is the number of bytes since the
  last latch that sets the receive pending (0: never). `OTCNT` is the idle
  time, in UART clocks (48 MHz from the PLL), after a byte that sets the
  timeout pending. The sources give no receive by `BUF` a byte at a time,
  no error flags (framing, overrun) and no `BAUD` formula (Q-12).
- Sources: the emulator model; SDK `include_lib/driver/device/uart.h`
  (that the receive is a DMA ring with a byte count and an idle timeout,
  not the bits); E-19, E-20 (fwtest behaves so).
- Standing: emulator-only
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-71: UART1's receive in fwtest
- Fact: In fwtest a `midi` byte arrives 320 µs after the one before it,
  whatever `BAUD`, `CON1`, `CLK_CON1` and the pins are set to: none needs
  setting. fwtest counts as "a MIDI receiver set up" (HARNESS, `result.json`'s
  `midi_bytes_dropped`) `CON0` with bits 0 and 6 set and `RXEADR` −
  `RXSADR` from 1 to 65 536. A byte arriving otherwise is dropped and
  counted: no interrupt, nothing in RAM, and `BUF` reads 0; fwtest has no
  receive through `BUF`. So does a byte with more than 3 125 waiting (about
  a second). Received bytes go into the ring as HW-70 says: a byte that
  arrives before the firmware has read the one before is kept; past the
  ring's size the oldest are overwritten, with no flag in `CON0`. The
  receive pending is set when the bytes since the last latch reach `RXCNT`,
  so a handler that clears it without latching gets it again on every
  later byte. The timeout comes `OTCNT` × 5 cycles (at 240 MHz) after the
  last byte, and at least one byte time (320 µs). Source 20 then interrupts
  as any source does (HW-20, HW-22). E-19: with `RXCNT` 4 and `OTCNT`
  48 000, six bytes from 3 ms give a receive pending at 4.28 ms with
  `HRXCNT` 4, and a timeout at 5.92 ms with `HRXCNT` 2.
- Sources: E-19, E-20; HARNESS ("Input scripts", "Outputs").
- Standing: confirmed (E-19, E-20)
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

  (the clock choices, the circular buffer, the byte count and idle timeout,
  the interrupts that can be left off).

### HW-69: UART1's receive flags, their acknowledge and the count latch
- Fact: In UART1's `CON0`, read: bit 14 is set when the receive DMA has
  taken the set number of bytes (receive pending), bit 11 when the line has
  been idle for the set time after a byte (timeout pending). Written as 1:
  bit 12 clears the receive pending, bit 10 the timeout pending, bit 13 the
  transmit pending; bit 7 latches into `HRXCNT` how many bytes the receive
  DMA has written since the previous latch, and `HRXCNT` keeps that count
  until the next latch. FM-1's own firmware receives MIDI from the jack
  this way, by DMA, on source 20.
- Sources: RE `docs/io/05-midi.md` §2.1 (the UART's flags at `0x00012100`:
  `0x4000` receive pending, `0x800` timeout; acknowledged with `0x80`,
  `0x1000`, `0x400`, `0x2000`; the count at `0x00012128` read in the
  handler); E-19 (the same bits in fwtest).
- Standing: confirmed (RE, E-19)
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-70: UART1's receive set-up bits, the ring, the count and the timeout
- Fact: In UART1's `CON0`: bit 0 turns the UART on; bit 2 enables the
  transmit interrupt, bit 3 the receive interrupt (bit 14, HW-69), bit 5
  the timeout interrupt (bit 11); bit 6 turns the receive DMA on. The DMA
  writes each byte at the next address of the ring from `RXSADR` up to,
  not including, `RXEADR`, and wraps to `RXSADR`; writing `RXSADR` starts
  it again at the ring's start. `RXCNT` is the number of bytes since the
  last latch that sets the receive pending (0: never). `OTCNT` is the idle
  time, in UART clocks (48 MHz from the PLL), after a byte that sets the
  timeout pending. The sources give no receive by `BUF` a byte at a time,
  no error flags (framing, overrun) and no `BAUD` formula (Q-12).
- Sources: the emulator model; SDK `include_lib/driver/device/uart.h`
  (that the receive is a DMA ring with a byte count and an idle timeout,
  not the bits); E-19, E-20 (fwtest behaves so).
- Standing: emulator-only
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-71: UART1's receive in fwtest
- Fact: In fwtest a `midi` byte arrives 320 µs after the one before it,
  whatever `BAUD`, `CON1`, `CLK_CON1` and the pins are set to: none needs
  setting. fwtest counts as "a MIDI receiver set up" (HARNESS, `result.json`'s
  `midi_bytes_dropped`) `CON0` with bits 0 and 6 set and `RXEADR` −
  `RXSADR` from 1 to 65 536. A byte arriving otherwise is dropped and
  counted: no interrupt, nothing in RAM, and `BUF` reads 0; fwtest has no
  receive through `BUF`. So does a byte with more than 3 125 waiting (about
  a second). Received bytes go into the ring as HW-70 says: a byte that
  arrives before the firmware has read the one before is kept; past the
  ring's size the oldest are overwritten, with no flag in `CON0`. The
  receive pending is set when the bytes since the last latch reach `RXCNT`,
  so a handler that clears it without latching gets it again on every
  later byte. The timeout comes `OTCNT` × 5 cycles (at 240 MHz) after the
  last byte, and at least one byte time (320 µs). Source 20 then interrupts
  as any source does (HW-20, HW-22). E-19: with `RXCNT` 4 and `OTCNT`
  48 000, six bytes from 3 ms give a receive pending at 4.28 ms with
  `HRXCNT` 4, and a timeout at 5.92 ms with `HRXCNT` 2.
- Sources: E-19, E-20; HARNESS ("Input scripts", "Outputs").
- Standing: confirmed (E-19, E-20)

---
name: perf-gate-steady-state
description: "Owner's 2026-10-22 decision on how the speed gate treats milestone work (startup vs steady state budgets)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d0aa28c2-493e-48cb-b0fd-be2a2d41a714
  modified: 2026-10-22T23:27:49.932Z
---

Decided by the owner in session M2 (2026-10-22): perf measures startup cost and steady-state cost per period separately (two run lengths; steady = difference; record both). Both get per-milestone budgets in config/budgets.json, raised only by their own PR with the reason, like code and RAM. The +3% gate applies only to steady state, between records under the same budget; startup has a budget but no 3% gate. R-PERF-2 amended in its own PR, before the M2 budgets PR.

**Why:** a new milestone's one-off startup work (e.g. M2 drawing the screen) would otherwise fail the +3% gate by design.

**How to apply:** when a milestone adds startup work, raise the startup budget in the budgets PR; keep per-period work within +3% or raise the steady budget in its own PR with the reason.

**M3 rule (owner, 2026-10-23; replaces the first-record rule of #39):** a main record is a speed baseline only if its firmware image SHA-256 differs from the image of the last record before the current steady budget was raised; records still holding that pre-raise image are skipped and named in the baseline note (perf.py choose_baseline). Reason: an unrelated merge (#43) landed between the budgets PR and the firmware PR, and records can be written out of order.

**How to apply:** a milestone raising steady needs only: budgets PR, then firmware PR, in any interleaving with unrelated merges.

**M5 (2026-10-23):** the baseline is chosen per budget *value*. A budgets PR that lowers a budget (M5 loaded 131 072 → 98 304) fails CI until main's image fits it, so the PR that brings the improvement (#66, the screen) must merge first. Then the budgets PR's record holds that image and is skipped as a baseline, so the next firmware PR's new, heavier measure is gated by the budget alone. Order: improvement → budgets → firmware.
