content.text: Now updating the M6a design notes for the receiver and the measured figures:

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md'; t=open(p).read()
old='''- Facts: none of the receiver's yet (SR-8, open when this was written);
  HARNESS.md's `midi` script event (a byte every 320 us). PROVENANCE P-38
  (what the spec and the SDK's header say so far), P-43 (the MIDI 1.0
  specification, as public literature).'''
assert old in t
t=t.replace(old,'''- Facts: HW-67 to HW-71 (SR-8's answer: the jack reaches UART1, received
  by DMA into a ring; the count latch; what fwtest counts as a receiver);
  HARNESS.md's `midi` script event (a byte every 320 us). PROVENANCE P-38
  (the request), P-43 (the MIDI 1.0 specification, as public literature),
  P-44 (SR-8's answer, read from its pull request, #81, before it merged).''')
old='''#### The parser'''
t=t.replace(old,'''#### The receiver
UART1's receive DMA writes the jack's bytes into a 256-byte ring of ours
(HW-70); `midi_start()` sets the ring and turns the UART and its DMA on
(`CON0` bits 0 and 6), which is what fwtest counts as a receiver set up
(HW-71). Once a block, before the engine reads MIDI, `midi_poll()`
latches the count written since the last time (`CON0` bit 7 into
`HRXCNT`, HW-69) and hands those bytes on. No interrupt: the engine acts
on MIDI once a block in any case, so one per byte would not lower the
latency, and polling keeps every MIDI change between blocks. More than
256 bytes between two polls (82 ms of the wire) would have overwritten
the oldest (HW-71); they are counted as dropped. Not set, because fwtest
needs none and the chip's are still open (Q-12): the baud rate, the
UART's clock, its pin and the port set-up. They come with real hardware.

#### The parser''',1)
t=t.rstrip('\n')+'''

#### Figures (fwtest 0.4.0, the branch at `02015ab`)
- **Latency**, from a note on's last byte to its first sample, 20 notes:
  1.718 to 2.897 ms, mean 2.308. By design at most two blocks (2.90 ms):
  up to a block until the engine's next callback takes the byte, then
  the block it renders plays after the one already playing.
- **The dense stream** (6 s of a full wire, 18 794 bytes, 3 272 note ons
  and as many offs on 16 voices): no byte dropped, no underrun, 48 571
  instructions a block on core 0 on average (the loaded measure's input
  takes 85 755). Its heaviest blocks are the panel screen's first whole
  drawing and the once-a-second heartbeat, both main's, as before M6a.
- **Cost at rest:** 1 838.6 instructions a block, 36 more than main's
  1 802.7 (+2.0%): the poll, its latch and the empty parse. Loaded:
  85 754.6, +1.0%. Code 18 352 bytes (+2 572), static RAM 143 256
  (+1 248: the two rings, the settings, the record, the hold table).
- **Every MIDI case's stream** gives the model's counters and messages
  exactly, junk and the SysEx flood included.
'''
open(p,'w').write(t+'\n' if not t.endswith('\n') else t)
EOF
tail -3 docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md

---
name: provenance-ids-race
description: PROVENANCE P-IDs and PR numbers collide with the spec side's open PRs; check theirs before numbering
metadata:
  type: project
---

M6a is built and all my PRs are green. **It isn't ready to clear yet**: #83 will conflict once the spec PRs merge, and this session needs to stay open to fix that.

## Decisions for you
1. **Should the loaded measure include MIDI?** Your panel test input plus dense MIDI take 109 899 instructions a block, past M5's loaded budget of 98 304; a wire filled to the last byte took 116 420. So I raised the budget in its own PR (**#86**: M6, loaded 131 072, nothing else changed). **#87** then adds MIDI to the loaded measure's test script. If you'd rather keep that measure panel-only, close both; #83 passes M5's budgets as it is.
2. **Program change and the mono/poly messages release held notes**, as PRESETS does. Keeping notes held across a mono/poly switch can leave stuck notes. Say if you want held notes to survive a program change.
3. **The receiver won't work on the real chip yet.** HW-70 is fwtest-only, and the baud rate, clock and pin are still open (Q-12), so none is set. The receiver is read once a block by rewriting UART1's `CON0` to latch the byte count; nobody knows yet whether that rewrite is safe on real hardware.
4. **The prompt's dense example can't happen on a real cable.** At 31 250 baud only about 2 notes fit in a block, so "all 16 voices retriggered every block" is impossible. The test fills the wire for 6 s instead, and all 16 voices sound.

## Merge order
1. **#80, #81, #82** (spec side). #82 already contains #81's PROVENANCE row.
2. **Tell this session "go".** #83 will then conflict on PROVENANCE.md and EXPOSURE.md. I'll merge main in, keep both sides, re-run the suite, push and report green.
3. **#86** (budgets; can merge any time before #87).
4. **#83** (MIDI in; depends on #81).
5. **#87** (MIDI in the loaded measure; stacked on #83 with #86 inside). I'll update it from main if needed.
6. I'll redo the drop from #83's merge commit and confirm the same SHA-256. Then "done, ready to clear".

## What M6a delivers
- **#83:**
  - **Receiver:** UART1, polled once a block. Latency from a note's last byte to its first sample is 1.718 to 2.897 ms; by design it can't exceed two blocks.
  - **Parser:** our own. Every MIDI test's byte stream gives exactly what a separate Python model of the same rules gives.
  - **Engine:**
    - notes held separately by panel, MIDI and sustain pedal, so neither ends the other's;
    - bend, vibrato, volume and expression;
    - all notes off and all sound off;
    - program change, the receive channel and the controller map.
  - **Screen:** MIDI's notes in cyan on the keyboard and on the event line.
  - **Tests:** nine MIDI test cases, R-MIDI-1 to R-MIDI-7, all passing.
  - **Speed:** cost at rest is +2.0% and loaded +1.0%. Every M5 budget holds.
  - **Docs:** PLAN.md records M6a's results and puts M6b (MIDI out) next, waiting on the spec side.
